meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 12: Transports & Protocol Utilities (multi-select)
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: Which statements about notifications in 2026-07-28 are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Change notifications arrive on the response stream of a subscriptions/listen request
notifications/message is delivered on the listen stream so clients see all logs
notifications/progress travels on the response stream of the request it relates to
A server may push any notification type it thinks the client will find useful
Every notification on a listen stream carries io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId

questions.explanation: Request-scoped notifications (progress, and logging's notifications/message) flow only on the originating request's stream. Long-lived change notifications come from subscriptions/listen, tagged with the subscription id, and the server MUST NOT send types the client did not request.

questions.question: Which behaviours are correct for a 2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP server? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Mint a session id and return it in Mcp-Session-Id on the first request
Answer an unknown JSON-RPC method with 404 and a -32601 error body
Buffer notifications for a request whose stream dropped, and resend them on reconnect
Answer an accepted notification POST with 202 and no body
Reject a request whose Origin header is present and invalid with 403

questions.explanation: A, B and C are spec behaviours. Sessions were removed, so a modern server never mints or echoes Mcp-Session-Id, and there is no redelivery: a dropped stream means the request is lost and must be re-issued.

questions.question: Which statements about promoting tool parameters into headers with x-mcp-header are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A tool that marks a number parameter is dropped from tools/list
Only string, integer and boolean parameters may be promoted
Any JSON type may be promoted as long as it is serialised first
Promoted values travel in the params object as well, for compatibility
Values that are not plain ASCII use the =?base64?...?= sentinel form

questions.explanation: The allowed types are string, integer and boolean — never number — and a server that violates that must drop the offending tool from tools/list rather than advertise it. Non-ASCII values are encoded with the Base64 sentinel; the value does not also travel in params.
